name: Zero-output refusals are not billed (Anthropic, from 2026-06-02)
reasoning: Anthropic's API release notes, 2026-06-02: "On the Claude API, you are no longer billed for a request when it returns stop_reason: 'refusal' without Claude having generated any output." Restated 2026-06-09 alongside the Fable 5 launch: "You are not billed for a request refused before any output is generated." Both fetched directly from platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api on 2026-08-12. This is not a lever anyone can pull — nobody engineers refusals — but it corrects an assumption a cost model can easily hold, which is the same shelf as the compaction entry. Identity is preserved structurally rather than by assertion: a refusal with zero output cannot differ in output from a refusal with zero output, so this does not rest on the provider's word about neutrality the way a batch-tier claim does. What DOES rest on their word is the zero itself; a usage report showing refusal events at $0.00 would upgrade the evidence from documented to measured.
savings: Not a lever. Removes a cost a model of the bill may wrongly assume.

name: Sonnet 5 introductory pricing became the standard price; the 2026-09-01 rise was cancelled
reasoning: Anthropic's API release notes, 2026-08-10: "The introductory pricing for Claude Sonnet 5 ($2 / $10 per MTok) is now the standard price: the previously scheduled increase to $3 / $15 per MTok on September 1, 2026 will not occur." Fetched directly 2026-08-12. Recorded as an entry rather than a footnote because this repo got it wrong in the most instructive way available: the errata table whose job is catching stale prices called the rise "the most time-boxed item in the register" on 2026-08-11, one day after it was cancelled, and src/rates.ts carried the post-lapse $3/$15 for three days — which over-stated Sonnet cost by 50% and every saving measured against it by the same margin. A cancelled future event is the failure mode a lapse date cannot see: lapsesDue() correctly reports a lapse that has passed and has no way to know one was called off. Only re-reading the source finds it.
savings: None. Prevents a 50% over-statement of Sonnet 5 cost and of every saving measured against it.
telemetrySignal: none — this is a rate-card fact

name: A PDF page bills twice: extracted text AND a rendered page image, unconditionally
reasoning: platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support, fetched 2026-08-12: "The system converts each page of the document into an image" and "The text from each page is extracted and provided alongside each page's image," with "Each page typically uses 1,500-3,000 tokens" of text on top of the image tokens. Both charges apply to every page of every document block; the docs offer no way to take one without the other. Like the compaction entry this changes nothing about the request — it corrects a bill the customer is misreading, and document-heavy workloads are exactly where a cost model built on text-token estimates diverges most from the invoice. The obvious remedy is NOT a lever and must not be published as one: extracting the text locally and sending it as plain text drops the chart, table and layout content the model was reading from the page image, so it changes what the model reads and fails the bar.
savings: None directly. Corrects a systematic under-estimate of document workload cost.
telemetrySignal: input tokens on document blocks far exceeding a text-only estimate

name: Citations: cited_text is free on output and on replay, but enabling citations adds input tokens
reasoning: The exemption is real and verified verbatim at platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations on 2026-08-12: "The cited_text field is provided for convenience and does not count toward output tokens" and "When passed back in subsequent conversation turns, cited_text is also not counted toward input tokens." Against a baseline of prompting Claude to quote directly, that is a genuine saving on quoted spans, compounding across a conversation. It fails anyway, and the same page says why: "Enabling citations incurs a slight increase in input tokens because of system prompt additions and document chunking." You can only collect the free quotes by changing what the model reads, and the comparison is therefore between two different requests, not the same request billed two ways — the exact pattern this register exists to reject. Filed as a rejection rather than dropped because it is the most persuasive near-miss found in nine sweeps, and an adjudication pass initially scored it PASS_ABSOLUTE by reading only the exemption sentence.
savings: Real against a quote-in-prose baseline; not identity-preserving.
telemetrySignal: input token delta on enabling citations for an otherwise unchanged request

name: Message Batches: errored, canceled and expired requests bill at zero
reasoning: platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing, fetched 2026-08-12, states "You will not be billed for these requests" against each of the errored, canceled and expired result types. Distinct from every registered batch entry, which all concern the 50% discount rather than the failure paths. No message is created on these paths, so there is no different-tokens, different-model or different-thinking question. CONTRACTUAL_ONLY on evidence class alone — this is Anthropic's documented policy, not a measured usage report, and it sits alongside the existing batch-discount entry which carries the same class for the same reason. Practically it matters most to anyone cancelling large batches routinely, where an assumed partial charge would distort the economics of the cancel-and-resubmit pattern.
savings: Unquantified. Removes an assumed cost on abandoned batch work.

name: web_fetch carries no per-call fee where web_search charges per use, and errored searches are not billed
reasoning: platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, fetched 2026-08-12: "Web fetch usage has no additional charges beyond standard token costs... You only pay standard token costs for the fetched content that becomes part of your conversation context," against web search's flat per-use fee, and separately "If an error occurs during web search, the web search will not be billed." Distinct from the registered entry on code execution being free when bundled with search or fetch, which is a different rule on the same page. The asymmetry is the useful part: a pipeline that already knows its URLs pays no tool fee at all, while the same work routed through search pays per use — and neither changes what the model reads once the content is in context. CONTRACTUAL_ONLY on evidence class: documented, not measured. Note that engineering search errors to avoid the fee is not a strategy and is not proposed as one.
savings: Unquantified. The per-use search fee, avoided where the URL is already known.
telemetrySignal: web_search_requests count against server_tool_use line items

name: The extended-thinking share of output is not recoverable from Claude Code transcripts
reasoning: usage.output_tokens_details is the only place the thinking share of output is reported, and it is absent from Claude Code transcripts. Measured on this machine 2026-08-12: 0 of 108,042 usage records across 1,661 transcript files carry the field. This is the one entry in the addendum that is MEASURED rather than documented, and it is the only class of evidence the register treats as stronger than a provider's word. Extended thinking bills as output either way, so no total is affected; what cannot be answered from this source is how much of that output was thinking, which on reasoning-heavy traffic is the question worth asking. A diagnosis about the instrument, not a lever — the same family as the register's other telemetry-gap entries. The tool now counts the field and states the absence rather than leaving the reader to notice it; the first implementation passed its unit tests and stayed silent on the real run, because cli.ts merged provenance by Object.keys over a literal that omitted the new counter.
savings: None. Bounds what the audit can honestly claim about reasoning spend.

name: Claude Code cache TTL flips from 1h to 5m on crossing from subscription into usage-credit billing; ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 restores it
reasoning: code.claude.com/docs/en/costs, fetched 2026-08-12: "The lifetime is an hour on a subscription and drops to five minutes once you're drawing on usage credits; on an API key or cloud provider, it's five minutes by default. You can keep the one-hour lifetime while drawing on usage credits by setting ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1." The boundary is the BILLING REGIME, not the auth type — a session that exhausts its subscription quota mid-day silently drops to 5m, and any pause longer than five minutes then reprocesses the full context at fresh-input rates. TTL is metadata the model never reads: same prompt, same model, same output, different bill. Distinct from the registered server-side TTL override entry (API-key auth granted 5m when 1h was requested): this is a documented, named boundary with a documented, named override. The audit's TTL right-sizing detector measures the opposite risk (1h bought where 5m serves); this is 5m imposed where 1h serves, and the fix is one environment variable.
savings: Traffic-dependent: every >5-minute pause in a long session re-bills the full context at 1x instead of 0.1x until the env var is set.
telemetrySignal: cache_read collapse after idle gaps of 5-60 minutes in sessions drawing on usage credits
